security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, Azure resource identifiers, and official documentation links. The permissive 0.0.0.0 firewall example is a confirmed medium risk because users may copy it into real deployments. I also found a medium semantic issue where a realistic password appears in a connection string example.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the 0.0.0.0 example with an approved private endpoint or least-privilege IP range, and add a warning before any broad access option.
Use an environment variable, secret store reference, or placeholder token in connection string examples instead of a realistic password literal.

remediation.issue: Command examples can trigger static review noise
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that package installation commands are optional documentation examples and should only be run after user approval.

content.value_statement: Azure MySQL Flexible Server setup is complex when teams must manage servers, databases, firewall rules, backups, and scaling. This skill provides focused .NET SDK guidance for common Azure Resource Manager workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation and Azure Identity setup for Azure.ResourceManager.MySql.
Explains the MySQL Flexible Server resource hierarchy and key SDK resource types.
Provides workflows for servers, databases, firewall rules, configurations, administrators, backups, restores, scaling, and deletion.
Summarizes SKU tiers, high availability modes, and production best practices.
Demonstrates connection string patterns, Entra ID token authentication, and Azure error handling.
limitations: Focuses on Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server, not Single Server.
Provides sample guidance, not a tested deployment for a specific tenant.
Requires Azure permissions, resource group details, and environment-specific network policy.
Does not replace Azure security, cost, or compliance review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Managed MySQL Deployment
use_cases.description: Design the .NET SDK steps for creating a Flexible Server with storage, backup, and high availability settings.

use_cases.title: Automate Database Operations
use_cases.description: Use Azure Resource Manager patterns to create databases, tune parameters, and manage lifecycle actions from .NET tooling.

use_cases.title: Review Azure MySQL Practices
use_cases.description: Compare planned firewall, identity, SKU, backup, and restore choices against the skill guidance before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Server Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a .NET plan for creating an Azure MySQL Flexible Server. Include packages, authentication, SKU, storage, backup, and high availability settings.

prompt_templates.title: Add Database and Firewall Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan database creation and firewall configuration for an existing Azure MySQL Flexible Server. Include safe network assumptions and required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my proposed Azure MySQL Flexible Server configuration for production readiness. Focus on identity, firewall rules, backups, HA, storage, and monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Design Restore and Lifecycle Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design .NET automation for backup discovery, point-in-time restore, scale changes, stop-start operations, and controlled deletion of Azure MySQL servers.

output_examples.input: I need to create a production Azure MySQL Flexible Server from a .NET service.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan covering packages, Azure Identity authentication, server settings, storage, backup retention, and high availability choices.

output_examples.input: I need to configure database access for a new Azure MySQL server.
output_examples.output: A workflow that separates database creation from firewall approval and highlights least-privilege network access.

output_examples.input: I need to restore an Azure MySQL server to an earlier point in time.
output_examples.output: An operations checklist for backup discovery, restore target naming, source server selection, restore time, and post-restore validation.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential and Entra ID authentication where possible.
Restrict firewall rules to approved ranges and prefer private network access.
Validate SKU, storage, backup, high availability, and monitoring choices before production use.
anti_patterns: Copying the sample password into a production connection string.
Allowing 0.0.0.0 without a documented security review.
Deleting, restarting, or scaling servers without backup and downtime checks.

faq.question: What Azure service does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server through the Azure Resource Manager SDK for .NET.

faq.question: Does it cover Azure Database for MySQL Single Server?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that Single Server is deprecated and focuses on Flexible Server.

faq.question: Which authentication approach is shown?
faq.answer: The examples use DefaultAzureCredential and also show Entra ID token authentication for database connections.

faq.question: Can it help with firewall rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows firewall rule creation, but users should replace sample ranges with approved least-privilege values.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy resources by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and sample workflow patterns for a user or agent to adapt.

faq.question: What should be validated before production use?
faq.answer: Validate identity, network access, backup retention, high availability, storage sizing, cost, monitoring, and compliance requirements.
